issues.legal_issue: Surplus land appurtenant to a textile mill constitutes an asset held in relation to the textile undertaking when it remains part of the company’s assets and is used to support the textile business, rather than belonging to a separate and distinct real estate business.
material_facts: The mill had been established on a large tract of land, and the company had not segregated the surplus land into a separate division or transferred its title.

The company had no separate capital assets or separate accounts for the alleged real estate division, and its financial statements did not distinguish that division’s land from the textile undertaking’s assets.
The company sold or developed surplus land to raise funds, and the proceeds were used to improve the textile business’s liquidity, pay its debts, and support its rehabilitation.
The company’s viability assessments treated disposal of the surplus land as necessary to make the textile undertaking viable.
issues.conclusion: The surplus land was an asset held in relation to the textile undertaking and vested in the Central Government; the appeals were allowed and the High Court’s contrary decision was reversed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(2), read with the definition of “textile undertaking” in section 2(d) of the Textile Undertakings (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1983, gives a broad scope to assets held in relation to the undertaking. A beneficent enactment should be interpreted to advance its purpose, consistently with Articles 39(b) and (c) of the Constitution. The relevant inquiry is whether the asset was held for the benefit of and used for the textile undertaking; sale or other use of an asset for a different purpose does not by itself sever its connection with the undertaking. The Court relied on New Satgram Engineering Works v. Union of India, [1981] 1 SCR 406, and Union of India v. United Collieries Ltd., [1985] 1 SCC 305, in applying a broad approach to identifying assets connected with an undertaking.

rule.if: appeal_over_asset_scope and land_appurtenant_to_mill and land_held_for_textile_benefit and proceeds_used_for_textile_business and not assets_segregated_into_independent_business

predicates.appeal_over_asset_scope: An appeal concerns whether land associated with a textile undertaking falls within the assets taken over with that undertaking.
predicates.land_appurtenant_to_mill: The company owned land appurtenant to its textile mill, including land not required for the mill’s immediate operations.
predicates.land_held_for_textile_benefit: The company held the land for the benefit of, or as a resource supporting, its textile business.
predicates.proceeds_used_for_textile_business: The company used proceeds from selling or developing the land to finance, sustain, or pay liabilities of its textile business.
predicates.assets_segregated_into_independent_busin: The company segregated the land and other assets into a genuinely independent business, distinct from the textile undertaking.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns the scope of assets associated with a textile undertaking, and appurtenant land was held for the textile business, its proceeds supported that business, and the assets were not segregated into an independent business, the land is included among the assets vesting with the undertaking.
